clue.text: See singer loosen up bra naughtily!

indicators.note: behaving naughtily means misbehaving, so the letters of the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: An exclamation inviting us to watch a performer undo an undergarment cheekily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link pointing to the example that follows; 'naughtily' rearranges LOOSEN UP BRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Robeson was a celebrated American bass-baritone vocalist and actor.

clue.text: Climber not quite getting to top of mountain

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the top of a mountain is its peak

explanation.surface: A mountaineer falls just short of the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims the last letter from PEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea plant is a climbing legume that clings to supports with tendrils.

clue.text: Extremist is some upstart lunatic in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution means turned round, so the selected run is read backwards
some means only part of the words that follow is used

explanation.surface: A radical is described as part of a crazed arriviste in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks ARTLU from upstART LUnatic, and 'in revolution' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is a person holding extreme views, especially in politics.

clue.text: Agent gets increased money for further performance

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
a rise is a pay increase

explanation.surface: A salesperson is given a pay boost for doing another show.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repeated performance or a return of a musical passage.

clue.text: Device for practical joke? Blunder getting person upset

parts.note: a boob is a silly mistake

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a party is a person, as in a legal document's 'the guilty party'

explanation.surface: A prank gadget goes wrong and annoys someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PARTY into YTRAP in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby trap is a hidden device set to surprise someone, sometimes as a prank.

clue.text: For example, a note giving authority

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example
so (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musical note given as an example carries official weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their permission or authority to act.

clue.text: When row follows end of honeymoon it's not so nice

indicators.note: end of means take only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A quarrel once the honeymoon is over makes things unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, meaning less pleasant.

clue.text: Told to select illustration

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the word sounds like the synonym that follows

parts.note: to pick is to select

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to choose a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pic is an informal word for a picture or photograph.

clue.text: Top person in attendance without identification

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so one word goes round another

parts.note: present means in attendance

explanation.surface: A leader turns up without carrying any papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a state or organisation.

clue.text: It's in her blood — in her cells too, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might take another arrangement

explanation.surface: Something runs in her blood, and in her body cells as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholesterol is a fatty substance carried in the bloodstream and found in cell membranes.

clue.text: Presumably in favour of authentic choral singing

definitions.meaning: read as two parts, against phoney, which presumably means favouring the genuine
responsive singing by two choirs alternating

explanation.surface: Genuine choral music presumably gets support.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is playful: 'anti' plus 'phony' would mean opposed to the fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiphony is alternating singing by two choirs or groups, as in church chant.

clue.text: Deal with pudding? Losing weight, take nothing

indicators.note: losing means the following letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: sweet is a British word for a dessert or pudding
o looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A dieter tackling dessert loses weight and eats nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' drops W from SWEET to leave SEET.
explanation.definitionFit: To see to something is to attend to or deal with it.

clue.text: Seriousness with which wine is poured into sauce

indicators.note: poured into means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: gravy is a meat sauce
it is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Solemnity as wine is tipped into the gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for Italian vermouth is a crossword convention from the drink gin and it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravity means solemnity or seriousness of manner.

clue.text: Henry leaving part of city to fetch the girl for a party

indicators.note: leaving means the named letter goes out of the word

parts.note: a ghetto is a district of a city
h is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
to get is to fetch
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: A man quits his neighbourhood to collect his date for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes H from GHETTO to leave GETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-together is an informal social gathering.

clue.text: Mineral woman keeps at home

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Olive is a woman's name
in means at home

explanation.surface: A woman stays indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivine is an olive-green silicate mineral found in igneous rocks.

clue.text: Food ready to eat after a short time

indicators.note: after places the ripe piece behind the time letter

parts.note: t is the short form of time
ripe fruit is ready to eat

explanation.surface: Something to eat will be ready shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is the stomach lining of cattle eaten as food.

clue.text: Gloss needed to make Bury more attractive, not half!

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: not half means only half the word is kept, its back half removed

parts.note: prettier means more attractive

explanation.surface: Something is needed to beautify the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in Lancashire, but here it is the verb. 'not half!' cuts PRETTIER down to PRET.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloss a text is to explain or interpret its meaning.

clue.text: Soldiers meeting something shocking? It's happening repeatedly

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
an electric current can give a shock

explanation.surface: Troops encounter something electrifying.
explanation.definitionFit: Recurrent means occurring again and again.

clue.text: Behaving abnormally, pet needs a medicine

parts.note: a cat is a household pet
taken as written
a tonic is a restorative medicine

explanation.surface: An animal acting oddly needs some medication.
explanation.definitionFit: A catatonic person is in an abnormal state of stupor or rigid immobility.

clue.text: Immediately in an awkward predicament

definitions.meaning: put in a difficult position, as when asked a hard question

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both instantly and in a tricky spot.

clue.text: English soldiers entertaining thin girl

parts.note: lean means thin
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: English troops play host to a slim young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor is a girl's name.

clue.text: Make provision for box that's moved right to one end

indicators.note: moved means a letter is shifted from its place in the word
to one end says where the shifted letter goes: the end of the word

parts.note: a crate is a box

explanation.surface: Getting ready involves shifting a box to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' names R, and 'moved ... to one end' sends it from second place to last.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater for is to make provision for, typically food.

clue.text: Provide a climax almost excellent

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to cap it all is to provide a climax

explanation.surface: Something nearly superb gives a finishing touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter from CAP IT ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is a dated British exclamation meaning excellent.

clue.text: Serious English composer, outwardly established

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so this abbreviation goes round the composer

parts.note: Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A grave English composer appears established on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and serious in intention.

clue.text: Blow that ultimately brings deformity

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so only the last letter is used

parts.note: a hump is a deformity of the back

explanation.surface: A blow that finally leaves a disfigurement.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a thump is a heavy punch or knock, the kind of blow struck with a fist.

clue.text: Local form of headgear still putting maiden off

parts.note: a topi is a sun helmet

indicators.note: putting with off means removing the named letter
off completes the instruction to take the letter away

parts.note: calm means still
m is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A regional style of hat remains, though the young woman is deterred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... off' drops M from CALM to leave CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine a topical treatment is local, applied to one part of the body.

clue.text: Plants seen in front of Coliseum before start of play

indicators.note: before places the first letter ahead of the act
front of means take the first letter of the following word

parts.note: Act I is the first act of a play

explanation.surface: Greenery is seen outside the Coliseum before a play begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are spiny succulent plants of dry regions.

clue.text: The woman's no backward "bird"

parts.note: her means belonging to the woman

indicators.note: backward means the following word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A woman is no slow learner, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: Continued working out of the public eye?

indicators.note: working means being worked on, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone carried on exercising in private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges CONTINUED; 'out of the public eye' is the definition, not part of the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnoticed means unobserved, not seen by anyone.

clue.text: Fellow who may be put on

definitions.meaning: a university teacher or fellow at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A man who might be teased.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university fellow, and to don is to put on clothes.

clue.text: Spin endlessly around in a groove

indicators.note: around means the remaining letters are read backwards
endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to turn is to spin

explanation.surface: Spinning endlessly round in a set pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TURN to TUR, which 'around' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rut is a groove, as worn by wheels.

clue.text: Monkey to hit something in the vegetable patch?

parts.note: to rap is to hit sharply
a scallion is a spring onion grown in a vegetable garden

explanation.surface: A naughty child strikes at a garden crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey is an affectionate term for a mischievous child, as is rapscallion.
